quandoUsar: Quick triage, one item at a time, where each deserves a moment of attention: selecting destinations, candidates, or design options.
Two-sided decisions (keep or pass) with undo, by dragging, with the buttons, or with the keyboard arrow keys.
Long decks: only four cards are mounted at a time.
quandoEvitar: Use `sortable-data-table` when people need to compare items side by side.
Use `carousel` to browse a set without deciding anything about each item.
Use `swipe-actions` for swipe actions on the rows of a list; here there are only two outcomes per card.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the stack (the outline appears on the top card) and then to the three buttons.
With focus on the stack, decide the top card to the left or to the right.
With focus on the stack, undo the last decision and bring the card back.
Trigger the focused button: reject, undo, or accept.

acessibilidade: The stack is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="card stack"` and a hidden hint with the keys; the top card announces its name and position (via `getLabel`) and the ones behind are `inert`.
Each decision, undo, and restart is announced in a `role="status"` region; `outcomes` supplies the verb of the sentence, but the rest of it (“3 left.”, “restored”) is fixed English.
The buttons use `aria-disabled` to keep focus when the stack runs out; the key hint, “Undo”, and the default empty state are also in English (`renderEmpty` replaces the empty state).
movimento: The top card follows the finger, rotates with the displacement, and shows the stamp of the chosen side; the ones behind rise gradually as it moves away.
Released beyond 35% of the width (at most 140 px) or on a fast swipe, it flies off with a spring in the direction of the gesture; before that, it returns to its place with a spring.
Undo brings the card back from where it left; with “reduce motion”, leaving and returning are just a fade and the ones behind swap places immediately.
responsivo: The stack is up to 20rem wide with a fixed height of 19rem (17.5rem on screens up to 26rem); the content of `renderCard` should fill 100% of the height.
On screens up to 22.5rem the undo button keeps only the icon, retaining its accessible name; the card uses `touch-action: pan-y`, so dragging vertically scrolls the page.
desempenho: Only the next four cards (and those still flying off) stay in the DOM, so the size of `items` does not weigh on rendering.
notasIA: `items`, `getKey`, `getLabel`, and `renderCard` are required; position is internal state and the parent receives `onDecide(item, "left" | "right")`, `onUndo`, and `onReset`.
Keep `items` stable: position is stored by index, so removing the decided item from the list inside `onDecide` makes the next card get skipped.
Handle `onUndo` and `onReset` along with `onDecide`, otherwise your list of chosen items diverges from the stack; `labels` names the buttons and the stamps.
